subtopic: Building insurance and an emergency fund
passage:
Friday night.
Every time Kishore asked if I'd started saving, I said, "After the next raise." Kishore asked twice this year, and I laughed both times.
Then the raises came. And the rent went up, I upgraded my phone, and dinners out became a weekly thing. The money vanished quietly, as always.
Today I woke in the night with a sharp pain and Kishore took me to the hospital. It was a short stay. The bill came before I'd left, and I had nothing put away. Kishore paid the difference without saying a word.
I'm glad I'm okay. I'm ashamed I had no plan. Tomorrow I'll write down what I earn, and what I spend.
— Keerthana

qa.q: How many times did Kishore ask about saving this year?
How does Keerthana feel about having no plan?
qa.a: Keerthana is ashamed, as the entry says, although also grateful and relieved that Keerthana is okay.

qa.q: What could Keerthana do first now that the bill is paid?
qa.a: Keerthana could start with a small fixed amount each month right away, and repay Kishore on a plan.

qa.q: How might Kishore have felt paying the difference?
qa.a: Kishore was probably worried and a little frustrated but chose to help quietly, since Kishore did not say a word.

grounding: The diary shows a person who keeps postponing saving until a raise while expenses rise, and a hospital bill arrives before any reserve exists.

subtopic: Building insurance and an emergency fund
passage:
Akash worked at the tea factory office in Munnar, and every year when appraisals came round he told his colleague Elizabeth the same thing: "Next year, after the raise, I'll start saving properly."
Each raise came. Each time, something grew to meet it: a better phone, a bike loan, weekend trips to Kochi with friends. His account still ran close to empty by the end of every month.
In the monsoon his father slipped on the wet estate path and broke his hip. The small hospital in town sent him on to a bigger one in Kottayam. The bill for surgery and ten days' stay came to more than Akash earned in three months. His father's small insurance covered only part.
Akash had nothing put aside. He borrowed from Elizabeth, from his uncle, from a moneylender his father had warned him about. Sitting on the hospital bench at night, he did the sums again and again. "After the raise," he said quietly to himself, "was always one year away."

qa.q: Where was Akash's father sent for surgery?
qa.a: To a bigger hospital in Kottayam.

qa.q: How did Akash feel on the hospital bench at night?
qa.a: Akash felt anxious and regretful, doing the sums again and again and seeing that saving had always been put off.

qa.q: What could Akash have done differently years earlier?
qa.a: Started saving a small amount from each salary straight away instead of waiting for a raise, so a reserve existed when the bill came.

qa.q: How might Elizabeth feel lending Akash money?
qa.a: Elizabeth is likely sympathetic and worried for Akash, remembering him saying "next year" every time.

grounding: It shows a young man delaying saving until the next raise, letting spending rise with each one, and facing a sudden hospital bill with nothing set aside.
